cites.quote: Doctor codes such as `D-0001` are display codes derived from row ids, not stored.
System lists normally answer `20 per page`; this endpoint is a stated exception.
The day schedule of one doctor and date is served from `api/src/routes/doctors.ts`.
A doctor, patient, department or specialization kept for history but not offered for new use.
then the order is dr. zed, Dr. Amy, dr. bob.
Entries with slot: null come last, ordered by name ignoring case.
Wherever entries are ordered by doctor name, names compare ignoring case

findings.suggested_fix: Use null-slot names where case changes the order, e.g. 'dr. amy' and 'Dr. Bob' (expect amy first). Add a null-slot tie with the same name to check the id order.
findings.text: S-3 AC4 cannot catch a case-sensitive name sort for null-slot entries. 'Dr. Amy' sorts before 'dr. bob' with or without case. No AC checks the doctor-id tie-break for null-slot entries either, though REQ-17 applies wherever entries are ordered by name.

cites.quote: D's only FREE slots are on 2026-10-26 (one day past today+6)
D's only FREE slots are on 2026-10-25 (today+6)
The window runs from now until the end of the 6th day after today in the hospital time zone

findings.suggested_fix: Pin the times: put a FREE slot at 07:30 local on 2026-10-26 (expect null), and one late in the day on 2026-10-25 after 08:00 (expect it returned).
findings.text: S-2 AC1/AC2 do not give the time of the boundary FREE slots. A now+7x24h window ends at 08:00 local on 2026-10-26. It passes AC2 when that day's slots are after 08:00, so the end-of-today+6 boundary goes untested.

cites.quote: An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason; its slot becomes free again.
Given D's first slot of the window is BOOKED and the next slot that date is FREE

findings.suggested_fix: Add to S-1: D's first window slot had a Cancelled appointment, so the endpoint returns that slot. Add a matching S-5 AC: the day schedule with a Cancelled appointment is unchanged.
findings.text: No AC covers a slot whose appointment was Cancelled. That slot is free again and must be returned. An implementation that treats any appointment as taking the slot passes every AC in S-1, and S-5 has no Cancelled case for the day schedule.

cites.quote: The hospital time zone is `Asia/Kolkata` (UTC+05:30 all year)

findings.suggested_fix: Say the offset comes from the fixed IANA Asia/Kolkata zone (no DST), or cite a context section that states UTC+05:30.
findings.text: Claim C1 adds 'UTC+05:30 all year' and the 00:00-05:29 date gap. The cited req claim C1 names only Asia/Kolkata. The offset is real-world tz data, not a value from the intent, so it is a derived value that the cited source does not cover.

rubric_items.reason: Stories S-1 to S-5 trace all 17 known REQs (REQ-1 to REQ-17). The intent has no assumed REQs.
Most stories carry one outcome. S-4 puts the unpaged list together with the error answers, and S-5 puts the privacy rules together with the no-change rule.
The ACs are Given/When/Then and S-2 AC4 is a good time-zone check. But S-3 AC4 does not test case-insensitive names, S-2 AC1/AC2 do not pin slot times, and no AC covers a Cancelled appointment.
The values are example data or derived inline: 21st doctor from 20 per page, 09:30 local = 04:00Z. The UTC+05:30 offset is not in the cited intent claim, which names only Asia/Kolkata.
The frontmatter and body agree and terms are used the same way throughout. The derivations are written out inline.
